key_insight: 360Anything lifts ordinary perspective images and videos into full 360° equirectangular panoramas without relying on camera calibration, by learning the mapping in image space using pre-trained diffusion transformers.
problem_solved: Removes the need for explicit geometric alignment and camera metadata when converting in-the-wild photos and videos into 360° panoramas, enabling panorama generation from uncalibrated inputs.
method: Geometry-free framework that learns to map perspective crops to equirectangular panorama space, avoiding explicit camera calibration or reprojection.
Built on pre-trained diffusion transformers to generate high-quality 360° content, adapted to handle both single images and sequential video frames.
Training and inference emphasize implicit spatial consistency (and temporal coherence for video) so outputs are plausible and seamless across the full panorama.
impact: Makes 360° panorama and immersive content generation accessible for real-world, uncalibrated imagery and video, simplifying pipelines for VR, augmented reality, data augmentation, and 3D scene modeling.
visual_elements: Before/after example: a perspective photo alongside the generated full 360° equirectangular panorama.
Pipeline diagram contrasting geometry-based (camera-calibration) methods vs the geometry-free diffusion-transformer approach.

paper_title: 360Anything: Geometry-Free Lifting of Images and Videos to 360°
paper_authors: Ziyi Wu, Daniel Watson, Andrea Tagliasacchi, David J. Fleet, Marcus A. Brubaker
